Rules extracted from the applications themselves, not from their documentation.

Each file in this directory records what one installed application accepts, the
version it was read from, and the exact command that read it, so the claim can
be re-checked rather than believed. The rule that makes them load-bearing is
spec section 5 of specs/PR-DESKTOP-APPS-CONFIGURE-SPEC.md: a desktop app keeps
its Configure button only where MCC's generated document is validated in CI
against a rule extracted from that app's own shipped code or published schema.

The precedent is tests/fixtures/schemas/, which vendors OpenCode's and Crush's
own published JSON Schemas. This directory is for the apps that publish none.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
roo-code-3.54.0.json
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
App:        Roo Code (VS Code extension, publisher rooveterinaryinc)
Version:    3.54.0, from its package.json "version"
Read from:  %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline-3.54.0
Date:       2026-09-12
Platform:   Windows 11, VS Code 1.136.1

Extraction (Git Bash; the bundle is one 14.8 MB minified line, so every read is
a grep for the identifier rather than a line number):

    EXT=~/.vscode/extensions/rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline-3.54.0

    # the settings key the extension reads at activation
    grep -o 'autoImportSettingsPath.\{0,220\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"
    grep -o 'roo-cline\.autoImportSettingsPath' "$EXT/package.json"

    # the shape of the document that key names
    grep -o 'providerProfiles:.\{0,160\}globalSettings:.\{0,120\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"
    grep -o 'currentApiConfigName:.\{0,200\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"

    # the apiProvider enum, in the five parts the bundle splits it into
    grep -o 'Htr=.\{0,700\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"
    for v in Qtr Btr uNi cNi dNi; do grep -o "$v=\[[^]]\{0,300\}" "$EXT/dist/extension.js"; done

    # the OpenAI-compatible profile's own keys
    grep -o 'openAiBaseUrl:.\{0,500\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"

    # openAiCustomModelInfo, and which of its members are required
    grep -o 'AP=[a-zA-Z0-9_$]*\.object({[^}]\{0,600\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"

Not extracted, and so not asserted: what Roo does with the profile *after* the
import. The import itself was not run -- that would write the user's own VS Code
SecretStorage -- so this rule says what the document has to look like to be
accepted, and nothing about what the extension then sends on the wire.
